about.title: The kind of engineer I aim to be
about.intro: These paragraphs are intentionally editable so you can tune the voice for internships, new-grad roles, or specific recruiter outreach without touching the layout.
paragraphs: I enjoy building software that balances product thinking with engineering discipline. The work I am most energized by usually sits at the intersection of clean interfaces, automation, and measurable impact.
My interests span application development, machine learning systems, deployment workflows, and the practical details that make a project reliable once it leaves the prototype stage.
I care about making technical work legible to other people. That means writing maintainable code, structuring information clearly, and leaving behind systems that teammates can actually extend.

skills.title: What I bring to a team
skills.intro: A recruiter should be able to scan this section in under a minute and come away with a strong signal on both technical depth and execution style.

items.title: Product-minded frontend and full-stack development
items.description: I like turning ambiguous requirements into clear interfaces, useful interactions, and implementation details that can survive real usage.

items.title: Automation, deployments, and engineering workflows
items.description: I pay attention to the path from local development to production, including CI/CD, static hosting, environment boundaries, and release reliability.

items.title: Data-driven problem solving
items.description: I enjoy projects that require debugging, instrumentation, experimentation, and turning raw system behavior into actionable next steps.

items.title: Clear communication and ownership
items.description: I value documentation, structured handoffs, and the kind of momentum that helps teams trust both the process and the outcome.

github.intro: The goal here is not vanity metrics. It is to show consistency, code review participation, and the shape of my output over time in a recruiter-friendly format.

leadership.title: Technical drive with community orientation
leadership.intro: I kept this section concise for recruiter audiences, while still showing that leadership and service are a meaningful part of how I operate.

highlights.title: Leading service projects at scale
highlights.description: I have coordinated people, logistics, and execution for service initiatives that required planning ahead, delegating well, and staying calm when details shifted.

highlights.title: Showing up consistently for others
highlights.description: Whether the setting is technical or community-based, I try to contribute in a way that makes the group more effective and the work more sustainable.

highlights.title: Making ownership visible
highlights.description: The same mindset that helps with service work also shows up in engineering: notice what needs doing, take responsibility, and leave things better than you found them.
